title: Local residue-field criterion for universal injectivity
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring and $u:M\to N$ an $R$-linear map. If $M$ is projective over $R$, $N$ is flat over $R$, and the induced map $M/\mathfrak mM\to N/\mathfrak mN$ is injective, then $u$ is universally injective: for every $R$-module $L$, the map $L\otimes_R M\to L\otimes_R N$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Tensor products have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: By [lem-trf-projective-over-local-free], choose a basis $(e_b)_{b\in B}$ of $M$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. There is no finiteness assumption on $B$.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, first proof sentence, invoking Algebra Tag 0593

proof.text: For finite $E\subset B$, let $P_E$ be the span of the $e_b$ with $b\in E$, let $a_E:P_E\to M$ be inclusion, and let $p_E:M\to P_E$ discard all other basis coordinates [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Since $p_Ea_E=1$, the same identity holds on the quotients modulo $\mathfrak m$, so $\overline{u a_E}$ is injective. It suffices to prove universal injectivity of every $v=u a_E$. Indeed any $z\in L\otimes_R M$ is a finite sum $\sum_t l_t\otimes m_t$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The union $E$ of the finite basis supports of its $m_t$ is finite, and $z=(1\otimes a_E)(z_E)$ for the same sum formed in $L\otimes_R P_E$. If $(1\otimes u)(z)=0$, universal injectivity of $v$ gives $z_E=0$, hence $z=0$. Fix such an $E$ and write $P=P_E$, with its finite basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, reduction to finitely generated direct summands, with the finite-support argument explicit

proof.text: Flatness of $N$ gives injectivity after tensoring the first map of a short exact sequence by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The middle exactness and terminal surjectivity follow from [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Thus $-\otimes_R N$ preserves short exact sequences, exactly the hypothesis of [lem-kun-lazard-flat-module]. Choose its small nonempty directed partially ordered set $I$, finite free modules $F_i$, transition maps $t_{ij}:F_i\to F_j$ for $i\le j$, and colimit maps $q_i:F_i\to N$. In particular $q_jt_{ij}=q_i$ and this cocone has colimit $N$.

By the representative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], each $v(e_s)$ is $q_{i_s}(y_s)$ for a stage $i_s$. Directedness gives a common upper bound $i$ for this finite list; for $r=0$, choose any $i$, using nonemptiness. Move the $y_s$ to $F_i$ and define $v_i:P\to F_i$ on the basis by these moved vectors. This gives $q_iv_i=v$. For $j\ge i$ put $v_j=t_{ij}v_i$, so $q_jv_j=v$. These identities also hold modulo $\mathfrak m$. Since $\bar v=\bar q_j\bar v_j$ is injective, $\bar v_j$ is injective for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, factorization through one finite-free stage and persistence of residue injectivity

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$. For every $R$-module $V$, the bilinear rule $\bar a\otimes x\mapsto ax+\mathfrak m V$ defines $k\otimes_R V\to V/\mathfrak m V$, with inverse $x+\mathfrak m V\mapsto\bar1\otimes x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The first rule is independent of the lift $a$; the second kills $\mathfrak m V$ because $\bar1\otimes bx=\bar b\otimes x=0$ for $b\in\mathfrak m$. The two composites are identities on the indicated generators. For a linear map $h:V\to W$, both routes send $\bar a\otimes x$ to $ah(x)+\mathfrak m W$, so these isomorphisms intertwine $1\otimes h$ with $\bar h$. In particular $k\otimes_R v_j$ is injective for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, interpretation of the reduction maps as residue-field base changes

proof.text: Fix $j\ge i$ and use the finite bases of $P$ and $F_j$ to apply [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization-strong] at the maximal prime $\mathfrak m$. Its residue field is $k$. It gives $a\notin\mathfrak m$ such that $(v_j)_a$ has a left inverse $s_j$. In a local ring the elements outside the maximal ideal are units. For any module $V$, localization at this unit has mutually inverse maps $V\to V_a$, $x\mapsto x/1$, and $V_a\to V$, $x/a^n\mapsto a^{-n}x$; the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] verifies the second is well-defined. They intertwine $v_j$ and $(v_j)_a$ on $x/1$. Composing $s_j$ with these two maps therefore gives an $R$-linear $s:F_j\to P$ with $s v_j=1$. For any $R$-module $L$, [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $(1\otimes s)(1\otimes v_j)=1$, so $1\otimes v_j$ is injective. This conclusion holds for every $j\ge i$; no compatibility between the chosen retractions is needed.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, finite-free split injections; the explicit finite-free form of Algebra Tag 00O0 (lemma-cokernel-flat)

proof.text: Fix any $R$-module $L$ and $x\in L\otimes_R P$ such that $(1\otimes v)(x)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], $L\otimes_R N$ with the maps $1\otimes q_h$ is the colimit of $L\otimes_R F_h$; switching the two tensor factors is the bilinear isomorphism $l\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes l$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The element $y=(1\otimes v_i)(x)$ in stage $i$ has zero image in this colimit. By the zero-detection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] there is $j\ge i$ with $(1\otimes t_{ij})(y)=0$. This is $(1\otimes v_j)(x)$, so step 6 gives $x=0$. Thus $v:P\to N$ is universally injective. This holds for every finite basis span $P_E$, so the argument of step 2 proves universal injectivity of $u:M\to N$, for every $L$.
